topic-05.meaning: “Pensel” denotes a graphite writing instrument whose marks can be erased, matching the proposed neutral sense. The term is also used in compounds such as “pensel warna” for coloured pencils.
topic-05.common_use: “Pensel” is established and understandable in Malaysian Malay, especially in school contexts. The supplied notes support ordinary usage but do not establish national frequency.
topic-05.preferred: Preference is not fully certain. “Pensel” is supported as a standard Malaysian Malay term, while “pensil” also appears in Malaysian commercial usage; the evidence is insufficient for a categorical normal-preference claim.
topic-05.register: Neutral everyday and educational; standard-dictionary usage.
topic-05.region: Malaysia; no narrower regional limitation is supported by the notes.

claims.proposition: In Malaysian Malay, “pensel” refers to a graphite writing instrument, including an erasable pencil.
“Pensel” occurs in ordinary Malaysian school-related expressions such as “pensel warna” and “bekas pensel”.

source_leads.lead: Indexed extracts from Kamus Dewan Edisi Keempat and Kamus Pelajar define “pensel” as a graphite writing instrument.
An indexed extract uses “pensel warna” and “bekas pensel” in a Malaysian educational activity context.
The product page uses both “pensil” in the heading and “pensel” in the description, indicating that “pensil” is also encountered in Malaysian usage.
